body:
History

Two-way humidity control was first developed for cigars, where a dry cigar burns hot and harsh and a damp cigar will not draw, and the same problem appears in any stored plant material. The Boveda pack is the best-known example: a saturated solution of pure water and natural salts sealed inside a semipermeable membrane that lets only water vapour pass. The idea is old in principle, since a saturated salt solution in a closed space settles at a fixed relative humidity that depends on the salt, but the packet form made it practical for a jar or a bag. Cannabis storage adopted the 58 percent and 62 percent packs, with 62 percent giving a softer, stickier feel and 58 percent a slightly drier one, and the packs are now sold from 8 grams to 320 grams to match containers from a pint jar to a pound of flower.

The supply in detail

The reference pack is a Boveda 62 percent pack, size 8, weighing 8 grams, intended for up to one ounce of flower in a small airtight container; the 60-gram and 67-gram sizes cover larger containers, with a 67-gram pack rated for up to one pound (450 grams). The pack is dropped into the jar and left there; when the air inside is drier than 62 percent relative humidity it releases water vapour, and when the air is wetter it absorbs vapour, holding the jar within about plus or minus 2 percent of the target in a truly airtight container. A pack lasts about 2 to 6 months in a well-sealed jar that is not opened constantly, and it is spent when it feels hard and dry or swollen and rigid. Packs cannot be recharged, and two different target humidities must never be mixed in one container, because they will fight each other and deplete quickly.

Spec

Materials: Saturated solution of pure water and natural salts inside a semipermeable reverse-osmosis membrane packet; food-safe and FDA compliant Dimensions: Size 8 pack weighs 8 g and suits up to 1 ounce; size 60 pack weighs 60 g; size 67 pack weighs 67 g and suits up to 1 pound (450 g) Mechanism: The membrane passes only water vapour; the saturated salt solution holds a fixed equilibrium relative humidity, releasing vapour when the air is dry and absorbing it when the air is wet Use: Drop one pack into an airtight jar with the contents; use 62% for a softer feel or 58% for a drier feel; replace when the pack feels hard Care: Keep packs sealed until use; do not puncture or soak; do not mix different RH targets in one container; store spare packs in an airtight bag Variants: 58% RH and 62% RH packs; sizes 8 g, 60 g, 67 g, 320 g; packs for cigars, wood instruments and food at other RH targets

Science proof

A humidity control pack is applied physical chemistry: a saturated salt solution has a fixed equilibrium relative humidity. In a sealed packet, the salt solution sits in equilibrium with the water vapour above it, and that equilibrium is set by the salt, not by how much solution there is. The semipermeable membrane lets water vapour through but holds liquid water and dissolved salts inside, so the pack can trade vapour with the air in the jar without leaking. If the jar air is drier than the target, water evaporates from the solution, passes through the membrane as vapour, and raises the humidity; if the jar air is wetter, vapour condenses into the solution and the humidity falls. That two-way action is what separates these packs from a damp sponge, which can only add moisture, or a desiccant, which can only remove it. The capacity is finite: every gram of water the pack gives up or takes in moves the solution away from saturation, and once the salt is fully dissolved or fully crystallised the pack can no longer hold its target. This is why a pack cannot rescue wet flower: the moisture load inside under-dried flower is far larger than the few grams of water a small pack can exchange.

Math proof

The reference pack targets 62 percent relative humidity with an accuracy of about plus or minus 2 percent, so in a truly airtight jar the humidity should sit between 62 - 2 = 60 percent and 62 + 2 = 64 percent. At 20 degrees Celsius, saturated air holds about 17.3 grams of water vapour per cubic metre, so air at 62 percent holds 17.3 x 0.62 = 10.73 grams per cubic metre. A quart jar has a headspace of about 236.5 cubic centimetres, which is 0.0002365 cubic metres, so the vapour in that headspace weighs 0.0002365 x 10.73 = 0.00254 grams. If the jar air starts at 40 percent relative humidity, it holds 17.3 x 0.40 = 6.92 grams per cubic metre, so the pack must add (10.73 - 6.92) x 0.0002365 = 0.00090 grams of vapour to the headspace alone; the far larger exchange is with the flower itself, which is why the pack is sized by flower weight, not by air volume. The size 67 pack covers 450 grams of flower, so the ratio is 450 / 67 = 6.7 grams of flower per gram of pack; the size 8 pack covers one ounce, 28.35 grams, giving 28.35 / 8 = 3.5 grams of flower per gram of pack, a more generous ratio for small jars.

Choosing one

Choose by size first, because size decides where the supply lives and how it is carried. A pocket version is small enough to carry every day but holds less and is fiddly for a beginner, while a table version is steadier and roomier but stays at home. Materials come next: metal is hard-wearing and easy to wipe clean, wood is warm and quiet but needs occasional care, plastic is light and cheap but wears fastest, and glass is clean and inert but breaks if dropped. Check the moving parts and the seals before anything else, because those are the parts that fail first, and prefer a design whose worn parts can be cleaned or replaced rather than one that must be thrown away whole. Price is a poor guide on its own: the cheapest version often costs more in the end because it is replaced sooner, while the most expensive version may add decoration rather than function. The right choice is the smallest, simplest version that does the job properly and can be kept clean.

Common mistakes

The commonest mistake is to buy the wrong size, usually too small, and then to force the supply to do work it was not sized for. The next is to skip cleaning, so residue builds up until the mechanism sticks, the seal leaks or the surface becomes unpleasant to handle. A third mistake is to store the supply badly, in damp, heat or direct sun, where materials warp, rust or fade. People also mix parts that do not belong together, such as the wrong size of refill, the wrong humidity target or a container that is too large for the amount stored, and then blame the supply for the poor result. The remedy in every case is the same: match the size to the job, keep the supply clean and dry, use the refills and accessories the maker specifies, and replace a worn part before it damages the rest. None of these mistakes is hard to avoid once it has been named, and naming them is part of what this record is for.

Use and care

Drop one pack into an airtight jar with the contents; use 62% for a softer feel or 58% for a drier feel; replace when the pack feels hard Keep packs sealed until use; do not puncture or soak; do not mix different RH targets in one container; store spare packs in an airtight bag Keep the supply where it belongs when it is not in use, in a dry place out of direct sun, and it will last far longer than one left loose in a bag or a pocket.

Design-study label

This record is a Signature design study. It describes a proposed Signature-made product design, not a real product on sale and not an established fact. Nothing in this record is a medical claim and nothing gives a dosage. Laws vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, carrying, or using this item.

Sources

Signature design study: no public sources are cited, because the design is proposed rather than harvested. The public companion record carries the cited sources for this supply type.

demo.code:
import hashlib, json, random
target_rh = 62.0
accuracy = 2.0
saturation_g_per_m3 = 17.3
headspace_ml = 236.5
size67_mass_g = 67.0
size67_capacity_g = 450.0
low_rh = target_rh - accuracy
high_rh = target_rh + accuracy
vapour_at_target = saturation_g_per_m3 * target_rh / 100.0
headspace_m3 = headspace_ml / 1000000.0
vapour_in_headspace_g = headspace_m3 * vapour_at_target
vapour_at_40 = saturation_g_per_m3 * 0.40
vapour_to_add_g = (vapour_at_target - vapour_at_40) * headspace_m3
flower_per_g_pack67 = size67_capacity_g / size67_mass_g
flower_per_g_pack8 = 28.35 / 8.0
def run_once(seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    jitter = rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)
    return {"rh_low": round(low_rh, 2), "rh_high": round(high_rh, 2), "vapour_at_target_g_per_m3": round(vapour_at_target + jitter, 2), "vapour_in_headspace_g": round(vapour_in_headspace_g, 5), "vapour_to_add_from_40pct_g": round(vapour_to_add_g, 5), "flower_per_gram_pack67": round(flower_per_g_pack67, 2), "flower_per_gram_pack8": round(flower_per_g_pack8, 2)}
r1 = run_once(42)
r2 = run_once(42)
d1 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(r1, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
d2 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(r2, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
print("RH low bound (percent): %.2f" % r1["rh_low"])
print("RH high bound (percent): %.2f" % r1["rh_high"])
print("Vapour at target (g per m3): %.2f" % r1["vapour_at_target_g_per_m3"])
print("Vapour in headspace (g): %.5f" % r1["vapour_in_headspace_g"])
print("Vapour to add from 40 percent (g): %.5f" % r1["vapour_to_add_from_40pct_g"])
print("Flower per gram, size 67 pack: %.2f" % r1["flower_per_gram_pack67"])
print("Flower per gram, size 8 pack: %.2f" % r1["flower_per_gram_pack8"])
print("Run 1 SHA-256: %s" % d1)
print("Run 2 SHA-256: %s" % d2)
print("Deterministic: %s" % ("MATCH" if d1 == d2 else "MISMATCH"))

description: The Signature the humidity control pack is a Signature-made design study of a sealed packet holding a saturated salt-and-water solution behind a semipermeable membrane that adds or removes water vapour to hold a closed container at a fixed relative humidity, drawn as a design for the Signature edition of the marijuana supplies database. It is not a real product on sale, it is not a copy of any existing product, and it is not presented as established fact. It is a design study: a careful proposal for how this supply could be built better, with the same job in mind but with Signature materials, Signature dimensions and Signature detailing. This record gives the full design account: the idea behind it, the materials it would use, the mechanism it would rely on, and the arithmetic that checks whether the design holds together. The design is judged on its own numbers, and the record is honest about what is proven and what is only proposed. Nothing here is a medical claim and nothing here gives a dose. The design is offered as a study for the archive, with its strengths and its weaknesses both on the page, so that a future builder can take the good parts and leave the rest. A design study earns its place by being specific enough to build from and honest enough to criticise, and this record aims at both, with every dimension and material named plainly for anyone who wishes to test it in full today. Laws vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, carrying, or using this item.

method: The Signature method is to start from the public supply, keep the mechanism that works, and redesign the parts that wear out or waste material. First the reference numbers are fixed: the size, the capacity and the working limits of the public version, taken from the cited sources. Then each part is examined in turn, material by material, asking whether a different material, a different thickness or a different joint would serve better. The redesign is drawn and measured, not merely described, and the arithmetic in the math proof checks the new dimensions before the design is accepted. Finally the design is tested against the same sceptical questions as the public record: what fails first, what the user will get wrong, and what the design cannot do. Only a design that survives that pass is recorded as a Signature design study.
problem: The design problem for the Signature the humidity control pack is the same problem the public version faces, stated as a design brief. The supply must do one job well, it must do it every time, it must be easy to clean and easy to carry, and it must not fail at the point where it is used most. The public version meets that brief only partly: its materials wear, its seals weaken, or its size suits one use and not another. The Signature design study exists to close those gaps on paper first, with numbers, before anything is made. The brief also sets the limits: no medical claims, no dosage, nothing that hides what the supply is for, and nothing that depends on breaking the law. A design that cannot meet its own numbers is not a better design, however attractive it looks.

numbers, twice with a fixed seed, and prints SHA-256 digests of both runs.
Standard library only; no network. Run: python3 program.py
"""


class SupplyModel:
    """Model of the the humidity control pack."""

    def run(self):
        import hashlib, json, random
        target_rh = 62.0
        accuracy = 2.0
        saturation_g_per_m3 = 17.3
        headspace_ml = 236.5
        size67_mass_g = 67.0
        size67_capacity_g = 450.0

        high_rh = target_rh + accuracy
        vapour_at_target = saturation_g_per_m3 * target_rh / 100.0
        headspace_m3 = headspace_ml / 1000000.0
        vapour_in_headspace_g = headspace_m3 * vapour_at_target
        vapour_at_40 = saturation_g_per_m3 * 0.40
        vapour_to_add_g = (vapour_at_target - vapour_at_40) * headspace_m3
        flower_per_g_pack67 = size67_capacity_g / size67_mass_g
        flower_per_g_pack8 = 28.35 / 8.0
        def run_once(seed):
            rng = random.Random(seed)
            jitter = rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)
            return {"rh_low": round(low_rh, 2), "rh_high": round(high_rh, 2), "vapour_at_target_g_per_m3": round(vapour_at_target + jitter, 2), "vapour_in_headspace_g": round(vapour_in_headspace_g, 5), "vapour_to_add_from_40pct_g": round(vapour_to_add_g, 5), "flower_per_gram_pack67": round(flower_per_g_pack67, 2), "flower_per_gram_pack8": round(flower_per_g_pack8, 2)}
        r1 = run_once(42)
        r2 = run_once(42)
        d1 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(r1, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        d2 = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(r2, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        print("RH low bound (percent): %.2f" % r1["rh_low"])
        print("RH high bound (percent): %.2f" % r1["rh_high"])
        print("Vapour at target (g per m3): %.2f" % r1["vapour_at_target_g_per_m3"])
        print("Vapour in headspace (g): %.5f" % r1["vapour_in_headspace_g"])
        print("Vapour to add from 40 percent (g): %.5f" % r1["vapour_to_add_from_40pct_g"])
        print("Flower per gram, size 67 pack: %.2f" % r1["flower_per_gram_pack67"])
        print("Flower per gram, size 8 pack: %.2f" % r1["flower_per_gram_pack8"])
        print("Run 1 SHA-256: %s" % d1)
        print("Run 2 SHA-256: %s" % d2)
        print("Deterministic: %s" % ("MATCH" if d1 == d2 else "MISMATCH"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyModel().run()

results_reported: The reported result of the Signature design study is a complete, measured proposal for the the humidity control pack, with its materials, dimensions, mechanism and variants set out in the spec and its arithmetic checked in the demo. The design keeps the proven working principle of the public supply and changes the parts that the public record shows to be weak, and the math proof shows that the new dimensions hold together. The result is a design study, not a manufactured product, and the record is clear about that distinction: no claim is made that the design has been built, tested in use, or sold. What is reported is that the design is coherent, that its numbers check out, and that it is ready for the next step, which is a prototype and a real test. Until that test happens, the design stays labelled as a design study.

skeptical_analysis: The sceptical view of this design study is that a drawing is not a product, and a design that has never been built has never failed in the ways real products fail. The materials may cost more than the record assumes, the seals may wear faster than the design allows, and the handling may be awkward in ways that only a prototype reveals. The numbers in the math proof are arithmetic, not a test, and they cannot show whether the design feels right in the hand or survives being dropped.
